rationale: Round 1 built and ran correctly with no ICE fallback, so this candidate raises obfuscation pressure on the strongest, lowest-risk passes: SUB gets the highest SecurityGain since instruction substitution is reliable and cheap for a tiny bit-manipulation kernel like drop3, complemented by strong BCF and FLA weights to obscure the bit-filtering control flow in drop_0xx and main; SPLIT stays moderately high because it is nearly free and synergizes with FLA by creating more basic blocks to flatten; IBR and ICALL are held at mid weights — they add meaningful indirection resistance on a 3-function program but carry higher correctness risk, and with only two real functions to protect the marginal gain does not justify aggressive settings; IGV is kept at the lowest weight since drop3 has little global state to encrypt and its dispatcher overhead would tax the hot bit-processing loop. RuntimeCost and SizeCost weights are kept below their security counterparts across all passes so the feature-driven selector still favors transforming functions whose features favor security/diversity, while CorrectnessRisk values remain conservative to preserve the round-1 clean build; overall this shifts the balance from 'compile safely' toward 'maximize resistance within proven-safe bounds'.
